In addition to Alexander Romanov’s ACL tear , four additional players have been on the injured reserve. However, on Sunday, the team shared encouraging news about three missing players who will join the California road trip this week. Current New York Islanders Injuries The injury wave began before the season began, as forward Mathew Barzal reaggravated a prior lower-body injury that kept him out indefinitely for the start of the season. item.title: Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase swap jerseys with Real Madrid superstar after NFL international game in Spain
item.description: Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals won the first ever NFL game in Spain thanks to Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase’s incredible connection. If the NFL wants to win over different markets around the globe, then sending the Cincinnati Bengals is a pretty good idea. Joe Burrow is on an incredible streak of form right now, and he led the Bengals to a 34-17 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Burrow threw three touchdowns in total. Wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase caught one, stacking up 155 receiving yards in total. The game was held in Spain, at the historic Bernabeu Stadium, home to soccer giants Real Madrid. After the game, Real Madrid’s star goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois posed with Joe Burrow and Ja’Marr Chase, exchanging jerseys. Soccer superstars attend NFL Madrid Along with Thibaut Courtois, Real Madrid stars Marc Cucurella and Eder Militao were in attendance, along with club president Florentino Perez. Spain World Cup winner Ferran Torres also linked up with Joe Burrow, greeting each other before the game. The Bengals’ victory strengthened their position in the AFC North, tying up their record to 6-2 to match the Pittsburgh Steelers. The Bengals host the Steelers on Sunday Night Football in Week 10, with the visiting team coming off a bye week. item.title: NBC Commentator Mike Tirico to Miss Sunday Night Football Game Due to ‘Health Issue’
item.description: Mike Tirico in Southampton, N.Y. in June 2026. Credit: Erick W Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty NEED TO KNOW Mike Tirico will miss NBC’s Bears versus Buccaneers broadcast because of an undisclosed health issue Noah Eagle will replace Tirico for the game at Chicago’s Soldier Field Tirico expects to return next week for the Steelers versus Bengals matchup Sports commentator Mike Tirico won’t be calling NBC Sunday Night Football’ s Bears versus Buccaneers game due to an undisclosed health issue. Tirico, 59, said in a statement on Sunday, Nov. 8 that he’d been sidelined due to his health, and Noah Eagle would take his place. “Unfortunately, I will have to miss tonight’s game in Chicago due to a health issue,” he said in a statement released by the network. “I look forward to watching tonight and can’t wait to be back with Cris [Collinsworth], Melissa [Stark] and the rest of our SNF team next Sunday night in Cincinnati.” He did not offer additional details as to his health issue. Mike Tirico in May 2023. Credit: Nathan Congleton/NBC/Getty Tirico is a play-by-play broadcaster for NBC, and has been the voice of Sunday Night Football since 2022, when he replaced Al Michaels. Prior to that, he spent decades with ESPN, and was the play-by-play announcer for Monday Night Football from 2006 to 2015. Tirico is also known for commentary on the Olympics and the NBA. Eagle, 29, is a play-by-play broadcaster for NBC Sports, and is in his fourth season calling the weekly primetime Big Ten Football game on NBC and Peacock. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to play the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on Sunday, Nov. 8. Tirico plans to return for the Sunday Night Football game on Nov. 15, which will see the Pittsburgh Steelers play the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium. In 2025, the broadcaster suffered an allergic reaction at the Kentucky Derby due to a lifelong nut allergy. item.title: Feyi-Waboso burns bright as England energy endorses Borthwick
item.description: "Plastic energy." That's what Bongi Mbonambi described it as. After scraping past Steve Borthwick's side in the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final, the South Africa hooker was scathing of England's back-slapping and celebrating of in-game wins. By then, it had already become something of a meme. Back row Ben Earl pumping his fist to celebrate Ireland's crooked line-out throw in a pre-tournament warm-up was a particular source of online mockery. But, while it isn't the diesel grunt that can win matches on its own, "plastic energy" is still something. It is the body language that shows mindset and intent, that a team's pilot light is on and burning bright. England had it under Borthwick at the Stade de France three years ago, coming agonisingly close to derailing the Springboks. And they had it in spades in Sunday's 45-22 win against the Wallabies. Earl, inevitably, was one outlet, loudly celebrating a third-minute scrum success. But there were plenty more examples throughout the match. Jamie George bellowing into the stands after the opening score; captain Maro Itoje being surrounded with congratulations after an early charge-down; Henry Slade being embraced after a lung-busting late try-saving tackle on Max Jorgensen. Borthwick needed it all. A report in the Times newspaper earlier in the week had said that a rift between the players and their coach opened in Argentina in July, at the end of the summer's campaign. England's senior players denied it. Nothing more to see, they said, than the transparent honesty of a team where input is valued and improvement is the lodestar. But, they also promised proof on the pitch against Australia. It was a risky gambit. Another misfiring, disjointed, underpowered performance – like that in their most-recent visit to Twickenham, February's 42-21 defeat by Ireland - would dial up the pressure on Borthwick another notch. Instead, his fired-up players turned up. They did so in the obvious ways. There was gainline physicality, breakdown bravery and crunching physicality. Ben Curry leaping out of the line to land a big hit on fly-half Declan Meredith was satisfyingly old school. But there was more than that. There was a different sort of bravery – the one that dares to chance the arm, throw a final pass and back ability, rather than take a safe option. Full-back George Furbank summed it up. Playing his first Test in nearly two years, his ball-playing smarts were summed up by a delicious involvement in Jack van Poortvliet's try, hitting a line, flashing a dummy and smuggling an offload to cut the Wallabies to ribbons. Henry Slade and Seb Atkinson pulled strings expertly as well. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso showed the sort of Test match mojo that England must protect at all costs. The Exeter wing, who, like Furbank, has endured a rotten injury run, was electric in the first half. Every time the 23-year-old touched the ball, expectation crackled around the stands. item.title: The Broncos’ fingertip interception was wild and shouldn’t have been allowed
item.description: The Denver Broncos have one of the most fearsome defenses in the NFL, not just because they hit hard, but also because they have ballhawks in the secondary. Denver entered its Week 9 matchup with the Carolina Panthers tied for seventh in the league in interceptions, and they added another one at the end of the third quarter in one of the wildest plays of the season for multiple reasons. Carolina QB Bryce Young threw the ball into the end zone for tight end Tommy Tremble, but it was successfully defended by Denver linebacker Justin Strnad. Tremble made a second effort to catch the ball, and it never actually hit the ground, staying in the air just long enough for Broncos defensive back Devon Key to grab it with his fingertips. It sure seemed like Key picked up the ball off the turf in real time. The Panthers lined up for the next play, and snapped the ball, running it with Chuba Hubbard. THEN the refs whistled and said they saw Payton’s challenge flag before Carolina snapped the ball, and reviewed the interception by Denver. It turns out Key grabbed the ball before it hit the turf, resulting in an interception. Watch the play here: Perfect place at the perfect time! Devon Key with an improbable INT for the @Broncos ! DENvsCAR on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AnjjfvlHFi — NFL (@NFL) November 8, 2026 Here’s another angle of the pick that clearly shows Key grabbed the ball before it hit the ground. That’s the real question. The refs’ decision to honor the challenge changed the game, because Denver went down and scored a touchdown after the interception. The Broncos just always seem to have luck on their side in the regular season. This is a ridiculous pick by Key either way.

Maryland’s captain Albi Ndrenika entered Sunday’s match with his offensive momentum at an all-time high, having scored twice in the previous three games for the Terps. Marco Wright made a brilliant run down the left flank before a give-and-go exchange, including a back heel pass from Lillian Fichelle, set Wright into space. The Werkself moved up to fifth in the Bundesliga table ahead of the international break while Cologne are 15th, just above the relegation places. Freiburg reclaimed third spot after Rani Khedira's own goal and Yuito Suzuki's fifth of the league season set up a 2-0 home victory over third-bottom Union Berlin. Vincenzo Grifo even had the luxury of missing a penalty. The Black Forest side, who went back above RB Leipzig, have never qualified for the Champions League but are well-placed after nine of 34 games. In Cologne, Leverkusen bounced back from losing 1-0 at home to Marseille in the Europa League on Thursday and two straight Bundesliga defeats. Garcia netted with a sumptuous free-kick on 7 minutes and Schick used his power to score on 85 having previously had a goal ruled out for a handball. "It was a great shot," García told streaming platform DAZN. "We practise in training when we can. This is something that I did all my career. Happy to score my first goal in the Bundesliga (this season)." Germany winger Saïd El Mala pulled one back in stoppage time, but it came too late for the hosts. Cologne avoided dropping deeper into the mire after second-bottom Schalke lost 2-1 at Hoffenheim in the late game. Strikers Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle were on target as the hosts surged up to ninth. Junior Adamu's late goal was Schalke's first in the league since October 11, but it was another day to forget for the promoted side. As far as the Falcons’ defense, they had a tall task going up against a red-hot Bengals’ offense, and Joe Burrow had himself a day, as well as Ja’Marr Chase. item.title: Hoffenheim claim 2-1 victory over Schalke after early Karius error
item.description: Hoffenheim claim 2-1 victory over Schalke after early Karius error Hoffenheim returned to winning ways in the Bundesliga thanks to goals from Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle providing a 2-1 win to see them head into the international break in 9th place. The match was also marked by injury concerns for Schalke, with both goalkeeper Loris Karius and Robin Gosens forced off during the contest. Hoffenheim made the perfect start when Asllani opened the scoring after just 10 minutes. Schalke goalkeeper Karius was at fault for the goal after attempting to play the ball out from the back, only to see his pass intercepted by the alert Hoffenheim forward, who guided the ball into the net. The visitors responded positively to falling behind, with Adil Aouchiche going close to an equaliser in the 14th minute. However, Oliver Baumann produced an excellent save to deny the Schalke attacker after Kenan Karaman had created the opportunity. Schalke's failure to take advantage of their promising start was punished when Hoffenheim doubled their advantage in the 26th minute. Following some patient build-up play, Tim Lemperle exchanged passes with Asllani before calmly slotting the ball past Karius to make it 2-0. Christian Ilzer's side continued to threaten before the break, with Alexander Prass firing narrowly over after being played through by Lemperle. Robin Gosens also had an opportunity at the other end, but his attempted volley failed to trouble Baumann. The second half began with a significant setback for Schalke. In the 47th minute, Karius produced an excellent save to deny Asllani, but the goalkeeper subsequently collided with his own defender Gosens as the latter attempted to reach the rebound. Both players required treatment and were unable to continue. Karius was replaced by Kevin Müller, while Vitalie Becker came on for Gosens in a double injury blow for Miron Muslić's side. Schalke nevertheless continued to search for a way back into the contest. Soufiane El-Faouzi came particularly close in the 57th minute, striking the crossbar after Baumann had initially saved an effort from Becker. Hoffenheim thought they had added a third goal shortly afterwards, but Andrej Kramarić was ruled offside. At the other end, Junior Adamu squandered a golden opportunity in the 72nd minute, firing wide from close range after his attempt was deflected by Vladimír Coufal. Schalke eventually found a breakthrough in the 81st minute. Edin Džeko's header was initially saved by Baumann, but the rebound fell kindly for Adamu, who made no mistake from close range to reduce the deficit to 2-1. The late goal gave Schalke renewed hope, but Hoffenheim managed to hold on during the closing stages to secure all three points. The result gives Ilzer's team an important Bundesliga victory, while Schalke are left to reflect on a frustrating evening in Sinsheim. item.title: Man United’s unique comeback leaves no one knowing how to feel
item.description: As the Manchester United players who had been told they were not fit to wear the shirt, in perhaps the earliest ever airing of that chant in footballing history, celebrated a second ridiculous comeback in five days, the Stretford End launched into a different chorus. They had told the team they were unworthy of representing them after a mere five minutes, had jeered in damning fashion when the dreadful Diogo Dalot was substituted, had been vitriolic about the Glazer family, Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. But United left the pitch in the relegation zone while their supporters serenaded Michael Carrick . “It’s hard to believe it’s not Scholes,” they sang. In one respect, it was hard to believe it was not Sir Alex Ferguson , plucking results from nowhere. In another, it was hard to believe this was not the prelude to a sacking. It may still be. Patrick Dorgu popped up to score an extraordinary stoppage-time equaliser (Reuters) But Carrick won’t quit. “That’s not going to happen,” he said. “I am quite clear what direction the club needs to go in and we need to win games.” They have only won once in 11 games, one point in three in the Premier League but Carrick is starting to specialise in escapology. Bournemouth had seemed the end for him, Roma looked it when his side were 2-0 down. Aston Villa seemed his valedictory game twice, before two two-goal comebacks. “Making it hard for ourselves,” said Carrick. That was putting it mildly. Yet his side have twice delivered a show of spirit to salvage something from the brink of humiliation. Ferguson’s most famous comeback was delivered by two substitutes, Teddy Sheringham and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. If Carrick has a lifeline now, it came from two replacements, scorers in Fergie Time, when it seemed time had run out for the latest United manager. First Patrick Dorgu set up Joshua Zirkzee to halve the deficit. Then Dorgu headed in Bruno Fernandes ’ 96th-minute corner. “In extra time conceding two goals is painful,” said Unai Emery . “Today we have lost two points.” Emery headed off for the tunnel when Dorgu scored, a picture of frustration. “I was angry with the situation, not with the players,” he said. A few minutes earlier, the Villa supporters had been jubilant, taunting their former midfielder Youri Tielemans with a chorus of: “Youri, what’s the score?” Few, Emery included, foresaw the eventual answer. Villa were on course for their biggest victory at Old Trafford since 1920; then, suddenly, they did not have a win at all. This was confusing and complicated, crazy entertainment. United showed a self-destructive streak at the start of each half and reacted to spread the kind of chaos that put a smile back on their faces. “I am disappointed we didn’t win the game,” claimed Carrick. United were both awful and exciting. They have character, if not competence at the back, where they did an impression of a particularly hungover pub team.
